content:
Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology
This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth
Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser.
The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. There are no other projects of its kind in the English language, and with two volumes already published, we hope to take this project to the next level. It's a rare look at Uyghur expression in an environment where all our stories are told by people pushing their own narratives without the intimate knowledge of our lived experiences.
<"Manifesto" by Sumayah Jurad from Vol. II>
We asked ourselves these questions - why wait for others to invite us to the table when we can pull up a chair and introduce ourselves? Why let others speak for us without trying first to speak? Our broken English can only be improved with audacity, and world literature is only enriched by the presence of new voices.
All-in-all, our efforts have been met with support from our community and pleasant surprise from those who did not know what they did not know.
Somewhat unprecedented is that we publish the authors' original language alongside the translation. Our book is filled with Uyghur, Latin, Cyrillic, and Chinese script to encapsulate as much of our community's experience as we can.
There are many publications in diaspora communities that platform East and South Asians, SEA, MENA, and more. Central Asia is often underrepresented in world literature or Asia-specific publications, and occupied territories even less so. Uyghurs themselves have been a relatively new diaspora community in English-speaking countries, and haven't had the opportunities to grow their literary or artistic communities. Many don't have the tools to nurture their talents, or knowledge of creative networks or opportunities, even when many journals seek work from underrepresented groups. In instances where they are aware, it's difficult to be published in this competitive field without the education and styles that publications look for. There are only a handful of literary translators translating from Uyghur to English, and not many Uyghurs who have had the chances to develop their creative language when learning English.
To sum up, the issues were:
No spaces for Uyghur writers and artists to develop their skills
A disconnect from artist communities, be it local or online
No bridge between our native tongue and English, and in turn, world literature
So, we put together a small group at the Tarim Network to take on this challenge. Completely volunteer-run; the very essence of a passion project. We did a call-out for anything and all. New writers, established writers, any language, any genre, whatever we could print in a book. And here we were, the first book of its kind, created to speak for ourselves without outsider voices, without a publishing house, raw and straight from the source.
<From the launch of Vol. I at Harvard University>
"The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a collection of Uyghur reflections in diaspora. Weaving together memories of the homeland, experiences of displacement, and transitions of identities, this anthology is a creative reflection of the beauty and complexities of the Uyghur experience.
By centering Uyghur voices at the forefront, this anthology serves as a form of living memory in a pivotal moment of Uyghur history. The title Under the Mulberry Tree refers to a story from the Uyghur literary classic Ana Yurt, where youthful Nuri faces terrible injustices, separation, and turmoil; but for one moment in the Charbagh, his love for Sebihe and his own family is full, ripe, and sweet, like the mulberries from the ancient tree. In a similar way that the mulberry tree offered comforts in Nuri’s time of need, we hope this volume offers a place of reflection and celebration of Uyghur culture."
We'd partnered with a member from a Jewish organisation to run writing workshops and explain editorial processes, as we had never worked on something like this before. After that collaboration, we decided to publish a revised edition on our own. This time, we added editors' notes to the pages to explain certain terms and historical and cultural contexts - mainly for our own youth, who don't always have access to cultural education. We translated more pieces from Uyghur and Chinese. Our contributors spanned 13 countries, at all levels of experience.
Was this work sustainable? Equipped with the tools, experience, and outpouring of support from our first volume, we spent the next two years saying yes. Our first book was now in libraries, there were articles and academic papers that mentioned it, and most of all, we reaffirmed the need for this sort of work. Not only were we accepting submissions, we worked one-on-one with emerging writers and artists to edit their pieces. We also helped first-time translators have their first publications with help from more experienced translators, as well as connecting them with the original authors.
Our second volume was even better than the last. From the blurb:
"How do we respond to the unexpected, and how does it influence perceptions of ourselves or the environments in which we exist? As a diaspora population, unexpected encounters can shape and transform what it means to be Uyghur as we build a new life outside of the homeland. Encounters Under the Mulberry Tree takes on the literal, abstract, and expanded renditions of these moments. We feature contemporary and historical works, including art, poetry, and prose in five languages with contributors based in a dozen countries, from established writers like award-winning author and filmmaker Tahir Hamut Izgil, to emerging artists, writers and translators of all ages. This book is a library of vignettes that grapple with intersections and how we make sense of it all."
Five languages (Uyghur, English, Chinese, Russian, Turkish)
<Vol. II showcased at a college hosted by Rawan Mentorship>
Now we embark on our third volume. The three of us do this while maintaining full time jobs, academic careers, and other side projects. We all live in different countries and have only met in person once. But it's something that we need to do, for our community and for ourselves. Our contributors have gained so much from this experience and we want to extend this opportunity to more people. This needs to survive in order for similar initiatives to be born.
Supporting the editors - all expenses so far have been paid out-of-pocket or through book sales. We do not have any donors or sponsors (yet!).
Supporting our contributors - we cannot afford to pay any of our contributors. Despite this, we have given free copies of the book to contributors, but this is definitely leaving a dent in our pockets.
Recruiting more people - paid internships or remuneration for one-off work would help volunteers spend more time on this project in this economy.
Enhance our level of expertise - we want to improve. Workshops or courses for our editors and contributors, professional feedback, the works. Unfortunately there is no one who speaks Uyghur and who is involved in Western publishing or English literature on a professional or academic level. We would appreciate connections with professionals from any language background, or the funding to level up.
Expand our network - we'd love to promote our work at literary festivals, go to conferences, do book events, establish ourselves in the public eye, provide reader copies to reviewers, and so on. However, there is a funding barrier to overcome to be able to attend these events, organise, or pre-order books.
<Vol. I on display at the Mosquers Film Festival, 2025>
Munawwar Abdulla is an Uyghur advocate, poet, and scientist born on unceded Kaurna land (Australia) and based in Massachusetts. She co-founded The Tarim Network, runs Uyghur Collective, and collaborates on projects with Uyghur rights organisations around the world. Her writings and literary translations have been published in places such as Modern Poetry in Translation, Asymptote, the Margins, the Georgia Review, and others.
Sonya Imin is a mixed Uyghur American scholar and multi-disciplinary creative who has worked on art and film projects across the US, Europe, and Central Asia. Growing up between the borderlands of the Uyghur homeland, broader Central Asia, and the midwestern United States, interrogations of belonging, home, and displacement influence the nature of her work. Currently based in Brussels, she is working on her doctoral research on Uyghur artistic production in the diaspora.
Maidina Kadeer is a mixed Uyghur-Hui writer and editor, born in Ghulja and currently based in Montreal (Tiohtià:ke), Canada. She holds a BA in English Literature and Law and Society from Concordia University, with a focus on post- and neo-colonial literature. Her work explores Uyghur identity, history, and culture through cuisine, agriculture, and neo-colonialism. She has contributed to projects such as a poem, NinetySix, in Slavs and Tatars’ Contest of the Fruits (2021) and participates in panels and interviews on Agriculture and Food History to raise awareness about Uyghur culture.

台湾欢迎4个盟友支持加入联合国气候谈判 - 聚焦台湾
台湾欢迎4个盟友支持加入联合国气候谈判
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月21日电 台湾政府周六感谢四个邦交国在最近举行的联合国气候会议上支持其参与全球气候治理，称它们的支持反映了对台湾为国际努力做出贡献的能力的认可。
危地马拉、伯利兹、圣文森特和格林纳丁斯、巴拉圭这四个盟国在11月17日至18日在土耳其举行的《联合国气候变化框架公约》第31届缔约方会议（COP31）高级别部分期间表达了对台湾的支持。
外交部在新闻稿中表示，各国支持台湾参与全球气候机制，并认可台湾在碳定价、温室气体减排、气候适应和清洁技术方面的努力。
外交部表示，危地马拉环境部长埃德温·若苏埃·卡斯特利亚诺斯·洛佩斯表示，台湾在碳定价、减排和气候适应方面的努力表明了其对气候中和的承诺。
圣文森特和格林纳丁斯表示，如果能源转型将小岛屿发展中国家抛在后面或将愿意合作的伙伴排除在外，那么能源转型就不能被视为公正或包容性。
巴拉圭在书面声明中表示，台湾在减缓和适应气候变化、技术发展和国际合作方面做出了重要贡献，应允许台湾参与会议活动。
外交部感谢四个盟友在重要国际论坛上为台湾发声，表示台湾在减排、气候适应、清洁技术和可持续发展方面取得了经验并取得了可衡量的进展。

Taiwan welcomes 4 allies' support for inclusion in U.N. climate talks
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 21 (CNA) Taiwan's government on Saturday thanked four diplomatic allies for supporting its participation in global climate governance at a recent United Nations climate conference, saying their backing reflected recognition of Taiwan's ability to contribute to international efforts.
The four allies -- Guatemala, Belize, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, and Paraguay -- voiced support for Taiwan during the high-level segment of the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), held Nov. 17-18 in Türkiye.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) said in a press release that the countries supported Taiwan's participation in global climate mechanisms and recognized its efforts in carbon pricing, greenhouse gas emissions reduction, climate adaptation and clean technology.
Guatemalan Environment Minister Edwin Josué Castellanos López said Taiwan's efforts in carbon pricing, emissions reduction and climate adaptation demonstrated its commitment to climate neutrality, MOFA said.
St. Vincent and the Grenadines said an energy transition could not be considered just or inclusive if it left small island developing states behind or excluded willing partners, according to the ministry.
In a written statement, Paraguay said Taiwan had made important contributions to climate change mitigation and adaptation, technological development and international cooperation, and should be allowed to participate in the conference's activities.
MOFA thanked the four allies for speaking up for Taiwan at an important international forum, saying the country had gained experience and made measurable progress in emissions reduction, climate adaptation, clean technology and sustainable development.

content:
射箭亚洲杯女子反曲弓决赛 台湾队负于中国队夺得银牌 - 聚焦台湾
射箭亚洲杯女子反曲弓决赛台湾队不敌中国队夺得银牌
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新网台北11月21日电 台湾女子反曲射箭队21日在中国杭州举行的2026年亚洲射箭杯金牌赛中直落三盘不敌东道主，夺得银牌。
台湾队由郭紫颖、李采璇和王芯柔组成，他们也与台湾射箭运动员林恩绮一起参加个人项目。
个人赛结束后，郭、李、王联手在四分之一决赛击败澳大利亚，在半决赛击败韩国，晋级决赛对阵中国队。
然而，台湾队却在五局三胜的比赛中，与中国队的李木子、沈佳雯、仲绮轩遭遇三连败。
台湾队以54-56输掉了首盘，王治郅第一箭只拿下7分，郭晶晶拿下8分。
第二盘，双方弓箭手各得一箭7分，台湾队以49-57落败。
第三盘台湾队有所进步，避免了低分，但中国队保持领先，以57-55拿下第一盘，以6-0锁定胜局。
作为台湾队最年轻的队员，王健林在金牌争夺战中表现不佳。
尽管她在三盘比赛中用六支箭两次击中10分内环，但她也打出了两支七杆和一支八杆，最终平均每支箭得到8.50分。
台湾队平均每支箭得分为 8.78 分，而中国队为 9.44 分。
中华台北射箭协会秘书长林政贤在评价球队的表现时表示，杭州射箭亚洲杯为射箭运动员提供了宝贵的经验。
他表示，在金牌比赛中感受到压力是很正常的，最重要的是在下一场国际比赛之前吸取经验教训。

Taiwan wins silver after falling to China in Archery Asia Cup women's recurve final
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 21 (CNA) Taiwan's women's recurve archery team won silver at the 2026 Archery Asia Cup in Hangzhou, China on Saturday, after losing to the host nation in three straight sets in the gold-medal match.
The Taiwanese team comprised Kuo Tzu-ying (郭紫穎), Li Cai-xuan (李采璇) and Wang Xin-ron (王芯柔), who also competed in the individual event alongside fellow Taiwanese archer Lin En-chi (林恩綺).
After the individual event, Kuo, Li and Wang teamed up to defeat Australia in the quarterfinals and South Korea in the semifinals, advancing to the final against China.
However, Taiwan struggled against China's Li Muzi (李木子), Shen Jiawen (沈佳雯) and Zhong Qixuan (仲綺璇), losing three straight sets in the best-of-five contest.
Taiwan lost the opening set 54-56, with Wang scoring just seven points on her first arrow and Kuo scoring eight.
Both archers then scored seven points with an arrow each in the second set, which Taiwan lost 49-57.
Taiwan improved in the third set, avoiding low-scoring shots, but China maintained its lead to take the set 57-55 and seal a 6-0 victory.
Wang, the youngest member of the Taiwanese team, struggled in the gold-medal match.
Although she hit the 10-point inner ring twice with her six arrows across the three sets, she also scored two sevens and an eight, finishing with an average of 8.50 points per arrow.
Taiwan averaged 8.78 points per arrow, compared with China's 9.44.
Commenting on the team's performance, Chinese Taipei Archery Association Secretary-General Lin Cheng-hsien (林政賢) said the Archery Asia Cup in Hangzhou had provided valuable experience for the archers.
He said it was normal to feel pressure during a gold-medal match and that the most important thing was to learn from the experience ahead of the next international tournament.

（中央社記者呂佳蓉台北21日電）華為常務董事長余承東20日在一場記者會上介紹L3自動駕駛路測時，宣稱「開車是可以睡覺的，別睡死過去就行了」，言論引起風波。他於記者會結束僅一小時後，馬上在微博發文說，目前仍處於L2輔助駕駛時代，駕駛務必專心開車、不能睡覺。
鴻蒙智行享界V8記者會20日在北京舉行，首款大型MPV「享界V8」正式上市，不過記者會上的焦點落在余承東的爭議言論上。
余承東在記者會上說，享界V8率先開啟時速120公里L3跨城高速路測，接著說「L3自動駕駛來了以後，開車就不用摸方向盤了，開車是可以睡覺的，別睡死過去就行了。20秒給你喚醒就可以了」，表示系統遇極端情況，會透過安全帶收緊與喇叭喚醒駕駛。
這番言論引起中國網友批評，有人說「依舊誇大宣傳」、「睡覺可不可以在家裡」、「為甚麼那麼執著於開車睡覺」，還有人批批評「符合現行法律規定嗎？大嘴一張，人命關天」。
隨著輿論迅速發酵，他於一小時後發文澄清，「有幾句話講的不準確」，說明V8目前開放使用的是L2輔助駕駛，L3硬體雖具備但尚未開放，呼籲大家握好方向盤，開車不能睡覺。
有相關報導指出，這並非余承東首次出現言論爭議。2025年5月，有網友發布影片表示，余承東駕駛問界M8時，頭部低垂近20秒且未握方向盤，質疑他「開車睡覺」。同年7月，余承東才回應稱「我當時是在低頭看手機」，並稱事後已主動前往公安局自首，接受罰款。（編輯：周慧盈）1151121

content:
韩联社首尔11月21日电 【要闻回顾】BLACKPINK成员Jennie获两项格莱美提名；韩国演员高庚杓承认醉驾并宣布暂停演艺活动；防弹少年团开启世巡“阿里郎”亚洲及澳大利亚站；NCT DREAM正规六辑销量破百万大关。
女团BLACKPINK成员Jennie凭借与澳大利亚迷幻摇滚乐队Tame Impala合作的歌曲《Dracula》，获得第69届格莱美奖最佳流行对唱/组合表演（最佳流行合作）与年度制作两项提名。其中，年度制作属于格莱美四大通类奖项之一。《Dracula》原曲于去年10月首次发行，今年2月推出Jennie参与的混音版后迅速走红，最高冲至美国公告牌百强单曲榜第三位。
此外，韩国女团IVE和KiiiKiii分别凭借《BANG BANG》和《404 (New Era)》，入围本届新设的“最佳亚洲流行音乐表演”奖。
演员高庚杓15日在其社交账号发文，就醉酒驾车引发交通事故一事道歉，并宣布暂停演艺活动。高庚杓于14日凌晨3时30分许在首尔麻浦区东桥洞酒后驾车，撞上环卫清洁车，当时他的血液酒精浓度达到吊销驾照标准（0.08%及以上）。
高庚杓出演的综艺节目《闲着干嘛呢》《第六感：B Side》《惊人的星期六》有待播出，他出演的《宝剑魔法》第二季和《大逃脱：都市怪谈》分别将于本月29日和下月2日上线。
防弹少年团（BTS）世巡“阿里郎”的亚洲及澳大利亚站演出19日拉开帷幕，整体计划在9座城市共举办26场演出。其中，亚洲站将于11月19日、21日、22日率先在高雄开唱，随后陆续登陆曼谷、吉隆坡、新加坡、雅加达、香港和布拉干，在7座城市共举办21场演唱会；澳大利亚站则将于明年2月在墨尔本和悉尼共举办5场演出。
11月21日的高雄第二场演出和12月29日的雅加达第三场演出将在全球80多个国家和地区的各大院线转播。
经纪公司SM娱乐16日表示，旗下男团NCT DREAM第六张正规专辑《DREAM AFTER DREAM》销量突破百万大关。
《DREAM AFTER DREAM》于本月9日发行。以韩国唱片销售统计网站Hanteo Chart统计为准，该专辑首周销量达到100.25万张，排名周榜第一。这是NCT DREAM自首张正规专辑以来，连续第11张销量突破百万张。该专辑在发行后席卷韩国主要音乐排行榜，还在QQ音乐和酷狗音乐排行榜取得亮眼成绩。

content:
经过一周繁忙的发射活动，本周全球发射清单预计将进行六次发射，其中包括范登堡发射的 3 次 SpaceX 猎鹰 9 号发射任务、中国的两次发射任务以及南美洲的阿丽亚娜 6 号发射任务。 SpaceX 将为美国太空部队和国家侦察办公室发射有效载荷，而本周的中国任务和阿丽亚娜 6 号任务中至少有一次将发射一批互联网卫星。长征2D |有效载荷未知，将于 11 月 18 日星期三从中国发射，长征 2D (CZ-2D) 预计将于世界标准时间 22:50 从太原卫星发射中心的 9 号发射场 (LC-9) 发射。官方警告通知表明发射轨迹是向南的，但有效载荷及其预定轨道的详细信息要等到发射后才会发布。两级、40.77 米高的 CZ-2D 由上海航天技术研究院 (SAST) 制造。 2D 版本不需要额外的捆绑式助推器。此次飞行将是长征2D的第108次飞行，也是今年的第七次。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-317 (R-6) SpaceX 将于 11 月 18 日星期三进行本周两次发射中的第一次发射，发射时间为四小时，发射窗口于太平洋标准时间晚上 7:00（世界标准时间周四 03:00）开始。
USSF-317 任务是美国太空军 (USSF) 本周的唯一任务，将从加利福尼亚州范登堡太空部队基地 (VSFB) 的东 4 号航天发射场 (SLC-4E) 发射，向东南飞行，将其机密有效载荷送入低地球轨道 (LEO)。所有系统看起来都很好，天气也有利于升空。猎鹰 9 号发射的 USSF-627 任务即将开始从加利福尼亚州发射推进剂 → https://t.co/IdlZbviZZl pic.twitter.com/fKxyN4DIui — SpaceX (@SpaceX) 2026 年 11 月 12 日助推器 B1100 将支持此次任务，这是自近一年前 11 月 23 日首次支持星链集团 11-30 以来的第十一次飞行， 2025 年。除了 NROL-105 和 USSF-385 之外，助推器之前的八次飞行支持了星链任务。 SpaceX 的西海岸无人机飞船 Of Course I Still Love You 将在 B1100 升空后约 8 分钟着陆时驻扎在地面。猎鹰 9 号是一枚直径 3.9 米、高 70 米的两级火箭。九台 Merlin 1D 发动机为第一级助推器提供动力，而第二级则使用一台真空优化的 Merlin 发动机。猎鹰 9 号和猎鹰重型火箭是第一批实现定期重复使用的轨道火箭，其中一枚猎鹰助推器已飞行 37 次。飞行后，两个有效载荷整流罩也被回收并重复使用。长征8A | SatNet LEO Group 本周的第二次中国发射计划于 11 月 11 日星期五举行。
世界标准时间 20 日 11:00，在中国文昌航天发射场的商业 LC-1 发射台上发射。长征 8A (CZ-8A) 将携带 9 颗通信卫星进入近地轨道，这些卫星由 SatNet 拥有并由中国卫星网络集团运营。 CZ-8A火箭有两个直径3.35米的级，总高度为50.54 m。第一级由两个捆绑式液体燃料助推器辅助。此次飞行将标志着 CZ-8A 的第 13 次飞行，也是 2026 年的第七次飞行。 NROL-136 SpaceX 本周的第二次猎鹰 9 号任务定于 11 月 21 日星期六太平洋标准时间凌晨 4:30（世界标准时间 12:30）发射，同样是从加州 VSFB 的 SLC-4E 发射。 NROL-136 任务将携带未知数量的有效载荷进入近地轨道，供国家侦察办公室 (NRO) 的增殖建筑星座使用，该星座由 Space 建造

【原文 English Original】
Following a week of busy launch activity, the worldwide launch manifest is set to see six launches this week, with three SpaceX Falcon 9 missions from Vandenberg, two Chinese missions, and an Ariane 6 mission from South America. SpaceX will launch payloads for the United States Space Force and the National Reconnaissance Office, while at least one of this week’s Chinese missions and the Ariane 6 will launch a batch of internet satellites. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload Wednesday, Nov. 18, will see a launch from China, with a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) expected to launch from Launch Complex 9 (LC-9) at the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center at 22:50 UTC. Official warning notices indicate a southerly launch trajectory, but details of the payload and its intended orbit will not be released until after launch. The two-stage, 40.77-m-tall CZ-2D is manufactured by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology (SAST). The 2D variant requires no additional strap-on boosters. This flight will mark the 108th CZ-2D to fly, the seventh of this year. Falcon 9 | USSF-317 (R-6) SpaceX’s first of two launches this week comes on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at the start of a four-hour launch window that opens at 7:00 PM PST (03:00 UTC on Thursday). The only mission for the United States Space Force (USSF) this week, the USSF-317 mission will launch from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) in California, flying southeast to place its classified payload into low-Earth orbit (LEO). All systems are looking good, and weather is favorable for liftoff. Propellant load is about to begin for Falcon 9’s launch of the USSF-627 mission from California → https://t.co/IdlZbviZZl pic.twitter.com/fKxyN4DIui — SpaceX (@SpaceX) November 12, 2026 Booster B1100 will support this mission, marking its eleventh flight since first supporting Starlink Group 11-30 nearly a year ago on Nov. 23, 2025. Eight of the booster’s previous flights supported Starlink missions, in addition to flying NROL-105 and USSF-385. SpaceX’s west coast droneship, Of Course I Still Love You, will be stationed downrange for B1100’s landing approximately eight minutes after liftoff. Falcon 9 is a 3.9-m-diameter, 70-m-tall two-stage rocket. Nine Merlin 1D engines power the first-stage booster, while the second stage uses a single vacuum-optimized Merlin engine. Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy were the first orbital rockets to achieve regular re-use, with one Falcon booster having flown 37 flights. The two payload fairings are also recovered and reused after flight. Chang Zheng 8A | SatNet LEO Group The second Chinese launch of the week is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, at 11:00 UTC from the Commercial LC-1 pad at the Wenchang Space Launch Site in China. A Chang Zheng 8A (CZ-8A) will carry nine communications satellites into LEO, with the satellites owned by SatNet and operated by the China Satellite Network Group. The CZ-8A rocket features two 3.35-m-diameter stages, with a total height of 50.54 m. The first stage is assisted by two strap-on liquid-fuelled boosters. This flight will mark the 13th overall CZ-8A flight, the seventh of 2026. Falcon 9 | NROL-136 SpaceX’s second Falcon 9 mission of the week is scheduled to launch on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 4:30 AM PST (12:30 UTC), again from SLC-4E at VSFB in California. The NROL-136 mission will carry an unknown number of payloads into LEO for the National Reconnaissance Office’s (NRO) Proliferated Architecture constellation, built by SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The booster supporting this mission will be B1097, flying for the 14th time. This booster first flew on Sept. 3, 2025, and has previously flown eight Starlink missions, as well as NROL-172, Transporter 17, Sentinel-6B, Twilight (Pandora & Others), and USSF-259. Following stage separation, B1097 will conduct a return-to-launch-site landing at Landing Zone 4 (LZ-4), located directly next to SLC-4E. Ariane 64 | Amazon Leo (LE-04) Amazon is continuing to put together its constellation of Leo satellites and will add another 36 on Monday, Nov. 23, at 10:12 UTC aboard an Ariane 64. The rocket will launch from Ensemble de Lancement Ariane 4 (ELA-4) at the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana, with the launch window lasting five hours and 27 minutes. Ariane 64 will follow a northeastern trajectory, delivering 22,000 kg of Leo satellites into LEO. Ariane 64 is a 62-m-tall, 5.4-m-diameter, expendable two-stage rocket built by the ArianeGroup on behalf of the European Space Agency. Both stages are powered by liquid hydrogen and oxygen-fuelled engines. The 64 variant of the basic Ariane 6 utilizes four P129 strap-on solid rocket boosters to provide additional lift-off thrust. This will be the fifth Ariane 6 mission of 2026. Watch the full replay of #VA269 . Relive Ariane 6's successful mission carrying 36 Amazon Leo satellites into orbit. First flight with P160C boosters Heaviest Ariane payload ever #LaunchingAmbitions #Ariane6 #VA269 @Amazonleo @ArianeGroup @esa @CNES @EuropeSpacePort pic.twitter.com/YLxW60wAo1 — Arianespace (@Arianespace) June 17, 2026 Falcon 9 | USSF-266 (TH-3) Closing out the week, a Falcon 9 launch is currently scheduled for Monday, Nov. 23, at 8:04 AM PST (16:04 UTC) — the third this week from SLC-4E at VSFB. The classified USSF-266 mission has a four-hour launch window extending to 12:04 PM PST (20:04 UTC). Falcon 9 will fly due south, indicating a polar orbit for the payload. While the payload is classified, the launch trajectory and other factors suggest that this may be an additional batch of satellites for the USSF’s Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator (SB-AMTI) program. These are based on the SpaceX Starshield satellite bus. The Falcon 9 booster supporting this flight will be B1081, making its 29th flight. B1081 first flew on Aug. 26, 2023, and flew four missions from SpaceX’s Florida launch sites before moving to Vandenberg for Transporter 10, where it has operated since then. The booster will land atop Of Course I Still Love You , stationed approximately 640 km downrange in the Pacific Ocean. If the current schedule holds, this will mark the 122nd Falcon 9 flight of 2026, and the 273rd orbital launch attempt worldwide in 2026. (Lead Image: Falcon 9 launches into the Florida morning skies. Credit: Julia Bergeron for NSF) The post Launch Preview: Ariane 6 to launch Amazon satellites, Falcon 9 to launch government missions appeared first on NASASpaceFlight.com .
